exposure: Pregnancy in women with WHO grade II glioma (GIIG)
Completeness of surgical resection (tumor residual volume)
Stability of oncologic status before pregnancy (tumor speed growth/stable lesions)
outcome: Glioma behavior change (acceleration of velocity of diameter expansion, occurrence of contrast enhancement)
Need for medical treatment and/or reoperation for glioma progression
cohort: Adult women (age <45 years) who had a histologically confirmed WHO grade II glioma resection and subsequently became pregnant with a stable oncologic status at the time of pregnancy.
finding: Patients who underwent a complete surgical resection and those with stable lesions before pregnancy demonstrated longer overall survival.
mod_finding: Deliveries were predominantly vaginal (all but one caesarean) and uneventful, with all children showing normal mental and physical development.
